editorial.headline: Private Education Beyond the Usual Curriculum
editorial.standfirst: This broad private-education activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked by Bali’s provincial PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned provider can register this activity in Bali today: nationally it is open to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the province-wide PMA moratorium. That clarity matters because the activity is deliberately broad. It is the home for privately run education and training that sits beyond the specifically defined education groupings, allowing a provider to frame a serious non-formal learning business around a distinct subject, professional capability, or practical skill.

Its reach extends from teacher and education-personnel competence development to professional-exam review courses, speed-reading instruction, safety-guard training, survival training, and public-speaking tuition. The scope also expressly includes courses in agribusiness, animation and film, broadcasting, journalism, maritime work, tourism and hospitality, agriculture, fisheries, livestock, public relations, entertainment, modelling, law, business law, tax law, and a range of cargo, travel, shipping, and hazardous-goods subjects. Education outside the school system connected with nuclear-energy topics is included as well.

This is therefore a category for private organisers whose offering is educational but does not need to be confined to a single narrow discipline. It also encompasses non-formal education units organised and managed through cooperation between an accredited or recognised foreign education institution and an Indonesian education institution, where that cooperation follows the applicable legal framework. Companies conducting training for personnel who respond to pollution in waters and ports also fall within its stated scope. The permitted business scales run from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah and Besar, giving the classification room for both a modest specialist course provider and a larger training operation.

The Bali position is unusually direct. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities. For this activity, however, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi or Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The result is not a Bali-side foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition hidden behind the national position: the record states a national ceiling of 100%, while Bali’s relevant conclusion is that the moratorium does not prevent PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, this activity is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium, while nationally it is open to 100% foreign ownership.
